questions.question: What is the name of a type of waterfall with an enormous volume of water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cataract**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cataract**:

 
 
• This term specifically refers to **a large, powerful waterfall with an enormous volume of water flowing over a steep drop**.
 
• Examples include **Niagara Falls**, **Victoria Falls**, and **Iguazu Falls**.
 
• The waterfall is **known for **having one of the **highest flow rates of any in the world**.
 
 
• In 2014, **Iguaçu Falls** recorded an all-time high in its flow rate, carrying 46,300 cubic meters per second - 33 times the usual water flow rate—after torrential rains.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cascade**:

 
 
• ​While distinct from other types, cascade waterfalls are **similar to multi-step waterfalls**. This waterfall cascades over a set of rock stairs, but unlike multi-step waterfalls, it lacks plunge pools at each step.
 
• This type is one of the more **common **along** seasonal creeks in hilly or mountainous areas**.
 
• **Roaring Fork Falls** in the **Pisgah National Forest **of western **North Carolina** is a perfect **example **of a cascade waterfall.
 
 
 
• **Rapid**:
 
 
• ​This term typically** refers to fast-flowing sections of a river with turbulence** and whitewater, not necessarily large waterfalls.
 
 
 
• **Chute**:
 
 
• ​This refers to **a steep incline over which water flows quickly**, often associated with artificial structures like hydroelectric dams.

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT** a metamorphic rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sandstone**__.

__
 
• **Sandstone is NOT a metamorphic rock**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metamorphic rocks are rocks that have become changed by intense heat or pressure while forming.
 
 
• In the very hot and pressured conditions deep inside the Earth's crust, both sedimentary and igneous rocks can be changed into metamorphic rock.
 
• ​Metamorphic rock can be formed locally when rock is heated by the intrusion of hot molten rock called magma from the Earth's interior.
 
 
• Some examples of metamorphic rocks are gneiss, slate, marble, schist, and quartzite.
 
 
 
• Marble, Slate, and quartz are formed after metamorphism. They changed in their original form due to extreme temperatures and pressure.
 
• The three types of metamorphism are Contact, Regional, and Dynamic metamorphism.
 
• Contact Metamorphism occurs when magma comes in contact with an already existing body of rock.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sandstone :
 
 
• Sandstone is a sedimentary rock composed of sand-size grains of mineral, rock, or organic material.
 
 
• It also contains a cementing material that binds the sand grains together and may contain a matrix of silt- or clay-size particles that occupy the spaces between the sand grains.
 
 
 
• Sandstone is a sedimentary rock composed mostly of quartz sand, but it can also contain significant amounts of feldspar, and sometimes silt and clay.
 
• Sandstone that contains more than 90% quartz is called quartzose sandstone.

questions.question: ______ has often been called the incubator of Western civilisation.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Mediterranean Sea:

__
 
• It separates Europe from Africa, through the Strait of Gibraltar.
 
• It connects to the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• It has often been called the **incubator** of Western civilization.
 
• This ancient "sea between the lands" occupies a deep, elongated, and almost landlocked irregular depression lying between latitudes and longitudes.
 
• It includes the Sea of Marmara and occupies an area of approximately 970000 square miles.
 
• To the northeast, it is connected with the Black Sea through the Dardanelles, the Sea of Marmara, and the strait of Bosporus.
 
• To the southeast, it is connected with the Red Sea by the Suez Canal.

• The Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden were formed as the Arabian plate separated from Nubia, as Nubia obliquely collided with the Eurasian plate.

 
 
• NE-directed extension between 35-27Ma leads to continental rifting along the line of the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
 
 
 
• The origin of the Red Sea's name is that it contains cyanobacteria called Trichodesmium erythraeum, which turns the normally blue-green water reddish-brown.

Caspian Sea 

 
• The Caspian Sea, which is frequently referred to as the largest lake or a true sea, is the largest inland body of water in the entire planet.
 
• An endorheic basin, it is located between Europe and Asia, which is bordered by the Caucasus Mountains to the east, the Iranian Plateau to the north, the rich plains of Southern Russia to the south, and the wide steppe of Central Asia to the west.
 
• With the exception of the extremely salty lagoon of Garabogazköl to the east, it has a surface area of 143,550 sq mi (372,000 km2) and a volume of 78,200 km3.
 
• The natural heritage of the Caspian sea is shared by five countries including, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Turkmenistan.
 
• Kazakhstan to the northeast, Russia to the northwest, Azerbaijan to the southwest, Iran to the south, and Turkmenistan to the southeast form the borders of the Caspian Sea.
 
• The Caspian Sea is famous for its caviar and oil industries and is home to a variety of species.

**Black Sea:**

 
• The Black Sea is in the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Which of the following is the new alluvium deposited by floods in the Ganga Plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khadar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khadar** refers to the** fresh alluvial sediment** deposited by periodic floods in the **Ganga Plain**.
 
• Also known as **"new alluvial soil," **Khadar is typically located in the floodplains of rivers such as the Ganges.
 
• It primarily consists of fine silts that are annually deposited by** floodwaters, **contributing to soil enrichment.
 
• Characterized by its fertility, Khadar soil benefits from the regular deposition of nutrient-rich sediments during flood events.
 
• It often exhibits a higher concentration of salts, derived from the river's water, which is replenished with each flooding cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Ganga Plain**, also referred to as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, spans approximately 700,000 square kilometers across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Encompassing regions of northern and eastern India, eastern Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the southern plains of Nepal, it stands as a fertile expanse.
 
• This vast floodplain is shaped by the convergence of major rivers, including the Indus, Brahmaputra, and Ganga, which traverse its expanse.
 
• Situated within the foreland basin of the Himalayas, the plain's landscape remains largely flat, characterized by soil deposits rather than mountainous terrain.

• **Bhangar **represents an older type of **alluvial soil, **characterized by its lesser fertility and sandy composition. Composed of aged alluvium, Bhangar soil tends to exhibit a darker hue.

questions.question: If the proportion of fine particles is relatively higher in soil, then it is called _______ soil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clayey soil **has a** high proportion of fine particles and typically feels smooth and sticky to the touch when wet.**
 
• Due to the fine particles,** clayey soil has small pore spaces, which reduces the rate of water drainage and can lead to waterlogging.**
 
• This type of **soil is often rich in nutrients because it can retain water and dissolved nutrients very well, although its poor drainage can sometimes be detrimental to certain plants.**
 
• **Clayey soil** is generally heavy and compact, **making it harder to work with, especially when wet.**
 
• Howeve**r, when managed well, clayey soils can be very fertile and are suitable for crops like rice that require a lot of water.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Soil Type
 Characteristics
 
 
 
 

 Sandy Soil
 
 
Sandy soil has a high proportion of sand particles and feels gritty to the touch.

 
It has good drainage and aeration but doesn't retain water and nutrients well, which makes it less fertile than other soil types.

 
 
 

 Watery Soil
 
 
This isn't a standard classification of soil. However, waterlogged soils can be an issue in certain situations.

 
These soils are saturated with water for long periods, which can deprive plant roots of oxygen and lead to the death of plants.

 
 
 

 Loamy Soil
 
 
Loamy soil is a well-balanced mixture of sand, silt, and clay particles.

 
It combines the beneficial properties of all these components, having a good structure, adequate drainage, and high nutrient and water retention. It is often considered the ideal soil type for gardening and agricultural uses.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a feature of 'soil'?

options.text: It is made up of inorganic matter.
It covers the surface of the earth.
It is a thin layer of grainy substance.
It is made up of minerals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **It is made up of inorganic matter.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Soil

 
 
• Soil is a combination of organic matter, gases, liquids, and organisms that support life.
 
• Soil is a living natural element.
 
• It is made up of both mineral and organic material.
 
• Soil properties are determined by the parent rock.
 
• Most soils have a dry bulk density of 1.1 to 1.6 g/cm3.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There is **8 main Type soil **:

 

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Found in the river plains and deltas of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus.
 
• Rich in potash but deficient in phosphorus.
 
• Suitable for crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil:**
 
 
• Also known as Regur soil, found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu).
 
• Rich in lime, iron, magnesium, and alumina; retains moisture.
 
• Suitable for cotton, known as "Black Cotton Soil."
 
 
 
• **Red and Yellow Soil:**
 
 
• Found in the Eastern and Southern parts of the Deccan Plateau (Odisha, Chhattisgarh, southern parts of the Middle Ganga plain, and along the piedmont zone of the Western Ghats).
 
• Rich in iron but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus, and humus.
 
• Suitable for crops like rice, ragi, tobacco, and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Laterite Soil:**
 
 
• Found in areas with high rainfall (Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, parts of Odisha, and Meghalaya).
 
• Rich in iron and aluminum but poor in nitrogen, potassium, and organic matter.
 
• Suitable for crops like tea, coffee, cashew nuts, and tapioca.
 
 
 
• **Arid and Desert Soil:**
 
 
• Found in the arid regions of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and the northern parts of Karnataka.
 
• Sandy and saline, low in organic matter and moisture content.
 
• Suitable for drought-resistant crops like bajra, jowar, and pulses.
 
 
 
• **Saline and Alkaline Soil:**
 
 
• Found in arid and semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Contains high amounts of sodium, potassium, and magnesium salts.
 
• Requires soil treatment for cultivation; suitable for salt-tolerant crops like barley, cotton, and sugar beet.
 
 
 
• **Peaty and Marshy Soil:**
 
 
• Found in areas with heavy rainfall and high humidity, such as Kerala, coastal areas of Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• Rich in organic matter but deficient in potash and phosphate.
 
• Suitable for rice and jute cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Forest and Mountain Soil:**
 
 
• Found in the Himalayan region, Western and Eastern Ghats, and some parts of the peninsular plateau.
 
• Rich in humus but poor in potash, phosphorus, and lime.
 
• Suitable for tea, coffee, spices, and temperate fruits.
